game: WAS @ DAL Week 7 2025, kickoff 2025-10-19 16:25 ET, roof closed, DAL -1.5, total 54.5

script.base: Books have a closed-roof pick'em shootout: DAL -1.5, total 54.5, implied DAL 28.0 / WAS 26.5, so both offenses stay on the field and neither side is a blowout. Dallas's pass engine is George Pickens (26 targets, 359 yards, 353 air in weeks 4-6) with Javonte Williams (49 carries, 249 yards) taking the late carries only if Dallas is up a score. Washington must manufacture 26.5 without Terry McLaurin and Deebo Samuel, so Jayden Daniels (17/92 rushing L3, and +0.39 EPA/db when blitzed) throws to the next men while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (38/219 L3) keeps a moderate carry share in a game that should stay within a score.
script.flip1: Dallas scores early, Williams closes on the ground the way his 49-carry L3 role allows, Prescott's dropbacks and Pickens's air yards stall, and Washington trails so Croskey-Merritt's carries die while Lane, Moore and McCaffrey targets spike.
script.flip2: Washington leads or trades scores into the 50s, both quarterbacks throw the whole way, Williams never gets the clock-kill bump (his 29-yard last-4 game is the template), and pass overs cash together while pure rush overs are ordinary.

injury_fallout: Source: nflverse pre-game injury report plus weeks 4-6 usage. WAS WR Terry McLaurin Out (quad) and Deebo Samuel Out (heel). McLaurin is absent from the weeks 4-6 target list, so his absence is already in the baseline; Deebo is the new hole (22 targets, 183 yards, 197 air in that window). Next men already on the field: Zach Ertz 11/64/77 but Questionable shoulder (snap-limit risk, do not bet him), Chris Moore 9/46/114, Jaylin Lane 7/71/117, Luke McCaffrey 6/104/140, Jeremy McNichols 8/42, Croskey-Merritt 5/56. WAS G Sam Cosmi Questionable (knee) is a rush-efficiency drag if he sits. WAS CB Jonathan Jones Questionable (hamstring) and DE Dorance Armstrong Questionable (hamstring) soften coverage and rush if inactive. DAL CB Trevon Diggs Out (knee) and CB Caelen Carson Questionable (knee) are the coverage loss Washington's remaining receivers face. DAL G Trevor Keegan Out (neck) and T Ajani Cornelius Questionable (knee) raise pressure and can cut Williams's efficiency. DAL DT Mazi Smith Questionable (ankle), DE Marshawn Kneeland Questionable (ankle), S Juanyeh Thomas Questionable (illness), WR Jonathan Mingo Questionable (knee) are unconfirmed. Final inactives (~90 minutes pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location only: DAL allows left 9.54 YPA (91 att), middle 10.97 (32 att), right 6.1 (82 att) — middle is a small-sample gash, right is the contained side. WAS allows left 7.9 (71), middle 7.79 (29), right 8.77 (84).
matchup.pressure: DAL blitzes only 24%; WAS EPA/db is +0.39 vs blitz vs +0.08 vs none, so Daniels is better when pressured and Dallas does not blitz often. WAS blitzes 32%; DAL EPA/db is +0.22 vs blitz vs +0.26 vs none, a small dip, not a pressure script that erases Pickens. Kneeland and Armstrong are both Questionable, so those blitz/pressure rates may come in light. No time-to-throw charting saved.
matchup.bleeds: DAL run defense is the clearest bleed: 4.96 YPC and 27 runs of 10+ in 6 games, plus 21 passes of 20+ for 216 yards, with middle/left the pass soft spots. WAS is leakier on explosives than on down-to-down YPA: 4.50 YPC, 20 runs of 10+, 19 passes of 20+ for 202 yards, worst YPA to the right (8.77).
matchup.overlap: Pickens is the confirmed primary (26 targets, 353 air L3) into a WAS defense that has allowed 19 explosives and 8.77 YPA right, with Jones questionable. On the other side the nominal primary (Deebo) is out; the overlap is the next man who already draws air yards — Lane 117 air on 7 targets, McCaffrey 140 air on 6 — against a Diggs-less secondary that has been gashed in the middle (10.97) and left (9.54).

form: Weeks 4-6 and last-4 logs, not season averages. Pickens last4 recyds 68, 134, 57, 168 vs a 68.5 stand-in median: mean far above the number, 2 of 4 cleared it; L3 is 359 yards on 353 air, so the yards are targets not one YAC fluke. Lane last4 -2, 18, 16, 37 vs 13.5 (3 of 4 over); L3 71 yards on 7 targets. McCaffrey last4 56, 21, 50, 33 vs 33.5, L3 104 yards on only 6 targets — efficiency without a proven target bump yet. Croskey-Merritt last4 rush 26, 47, 111, 61 and rush+rec 31, 57, 150, 68; L3 38/219. Williams last4 rush 76, 85, 135, 29 vs 80.5, L3 49/249, sitting on his median. Sanders is missing from the weeks 4-6 rusher list (Williams 49, Blue 7, Prescott 6, Flournoy 4) despite last4 rush 53, 15, 41, 8. Lamb has only 2 games (110, 112) against 111.5. Ertz last4 38, 21, 0, 43 with a shoulder tag. Rodriguez L3 12/66 against a 39.5 median.

pro_edge.sleepers: Ruled out, same-position lines unmoved: WAS WR Terry McLaurin Out and Deebo Samuel Out — teammates Jaylin Lane recyds 13.5, Luke McCaffrey recyds 33.5, Chris Moore recyds 25.5, and Zach Ertz recyds 32.5 are still season medians (Ertz also Questionable, not a confirmed out). No DAL RB is out, so Miles Sanders's 28.5 median is a role-lag candidate (absent from weeks 4-6 carries) but not an injury sleeper, and a healthy-scratch would void rather than cash an under.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Jaylin Lane's 13.5 receiving-yard median has not moved for Deebo Samuel's 22 targets and 183 yards leaving the lineup, and Lane already produced 71 yards on 7 targets over the last three games against a Dallas secondary missing Trevon Diggs that has allowed 10.97 YPA in the middle and 9.54 to the left.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the card lost. Lane lost because the Deebo vacancy (22 targets, 183 yards) went to Ertz, who played through the shoulder, and to Chris Moore, who already had 9 targets, while Lane repeated the -2 game — there is no chart proving Lane, not Moore, is the one attacking the middle/left bleed. Pickens lost because Dallas led, Trevor Keegan's absence muddied the pocket, and the staff fed Javonte Williams, so Pickens posted the 57-yard floor already in the last four; Lamb's 110 and 112 in his only two games took the share a 68.5 median was quietly respecting. A second way both lose: the 54.5 is dead air and the air yards (Pickens 353, Lane 117) do not convert. That counter-case is as strong as the read on Pickens and weaker on Lane, which is why Pickens is a flagged lean and Lane is the strong leg.
slip_story: One script only: closed-roof shootout, DAL 28.0 / WAS 26.5, spread 1.5 so starters finish. The two-leg stack is pass volume on both sides — Lane over as the unmoved-median next man after Deebo and McLaurin, Pickens over as Dallas's primary in the same high total. They win together if both teams throw. Not paired with a total under, a Williams rush over (needs the clock-kill flip), or a second WAS depth receiver (McCaffrey or Moore would cannibalize Lane). Croskey-Merritt rush over was the other real bleed (DAL 4.96 YPC, 27 runs of 10+, his L3 73 rush yards vs a 54.5 median) but it dies on the trail flip and fights Cosmi's knee, so it stays off this slip. No TDs. No bet placed.
